# Mask prevalence — EDM / FLM / WBM on a global tile sample

<!-- GENERATED by `python -m dataset.prevalence`. Do not hand-edit numbers; re-run to refresh. -->

Resolves issue #19 (part of the Phase-A map, #13). Measures the fraction of pixels per **EDM code** and **FLM source**, plus **WBM** water, on the deterministic 500-tile prevalence sample (`dataset.sampling.prevalence_sample`, seed `0xdeae`), read **full resolution** (spec §7 — ×8 overviews erase rare codes). Fractions are **pixel-pooled** across tiles, not per-cell averages (plan §A1 ⚠️).

- Tiles measured: **500** of 500 requested.
- Total pixels pooled: **4,265,568,000**.
- §6.1 cross-mask identities hold on **500/500** pooled tiles (a violation excludes the tile from the table — see anomalies).
- Provenance: code `84c5fcb-dirty`, snapshot `2026-07-17`.

## 3. Geographic structure

The issue asks specifically whether voids concentrate in steep forested regions `[verified]` (plan §11.3). **The direct answer: there is no void concentration to find — EDM/FLM void (code 0) is 0 on every tile in the sample** (§1 tables; the void branch of the binning is untested by real data because edited GLO-30 has effectively none). So the §11.3 worry, as posed about *voids*, is empty for this corpus.

The live concentration is instead *external fill and editing*. Terrain type has no name-level proxy and cannot have one — it is defined by the very metrics Phase A calibrates (#15) — so this sample cannot be stratified by forest/steepness before those metrics exist. Latitude band is the axis available at name level, and it already surfaces the real risk: editing spikes at the pole (ice-sheet smoothing), not in the mid-latitude forest belt.

## 4. What the plan's default gates would cost

Applying the plan's Phase-C defaults to this sample **without re-tuning them** (that is Phase C): WBM water > 0.30 drop, EDM/FLM-edited > 0.25 drop.

| Gate | tiles dropped | fraction of sample |
|---|---:|---:|
| WBM water > 0.30 | 202 | 0.4040 |
| EDM/FLM-edited > 0.25 | 17 | 0.0340 |
| **either (union)** | **219** | **0.4380** |
| WBM water > 0.05 (flag, not drop) | 248 | 0.4960 |

## 5. Resolution — does prevalence force the WBM-only fallback?

**No. EDM/FLM gating is affordable; the WBM-only fallback graduates into a decision to *keep* EDM/FLM columns.** The map's only live trigger was prevalence showing the thresholds cost unacceptable coverage (mask access itself is free — #14). Against this sample it does not:

- **EDM/FLM editing is modest and does not hollow out terrain broadly.** Only **17/500** tiles (3.4%) exceed the 0.25 edit/fill cap, and they are **not spread across terrain**: editing concentrates in the **85-90° band** (36.2% pooled), driven by EDM code 4 (*Smoothed*) over the polar ice sheets — a single stratum, not the steep-forest voids the plan's §11.3 risk anticipated. External fill (FLM ≥ 3) pools to just **0.80%** globally; its worst single tile is **25.2%**.
- **The WBM drops are whole mostly-ocean tiles, not terrain.** Of the **202** tiles over the 0.30 water cap, **128** are ≥90% water — coastal/island cells that survive discovery's absent-prefix filter and that the exact-zero ocean gate (ADR-0001 §3, ≥0.75 drop) already removes. ⚠️ This table is **per whole 1° tile**; Phase C gates score 224² **windows**, so a half-ocean tile contributes ocean windows (dropped anyway) and land windows (kept). The **40%** whole-tile water figure therefore **overstates** per-window land attrition — read it as an upper bound, not the Phase-C number.
- **The two gates are near-disjoint** (**0** tiles dropped by both): water is a coastline/ocean concern, editing a polar-ice concern. They gate different strata and neither compounds the other.
- **Voids are absent.** EDM/FLM void (code 0) never exceeded **0.00%** on any tile — in practice **0** across the sample — resolving the spec's fog note 3 (the void branch of the binning is untested by real data because GLO-30 has effectively none). The national-DEM fills (FLM 100–102) and TerraSAR-X (FLM 8) are likewise negligible.

**Carried to Phase C, not decided here** (threshold *values* are Phase C): the polar-ice stratum (85-90°) is where a strict EDM cap bites — flag it for the §11.3 attrition-by-stratum table so ice-sheet terrain is not silently hollowed out.

**Left open — a separate fog note, not this ticket's** (#13): whether `WBM == 1` should *supersede* ADR-0001 §3's exact-zero exclusion as the ocean test. This ticket measured WBM water fractions (§1, §3), which is the input that fog was waiting on, but does **not** settle it: deciding it needs a per-pixel `WBM == 1` vs `elevation == 0` disagreement count (how much land the zero-test mislabels — e.g. the Netherlands −12 m case), and this pass reads masks only, never DEM elevation. That comparison is its own measurement.
